title: Action triggers with claim windows for reactive turns
description:
Add a triggers system to game definitions that inserts claim windows after specific actions, enabling reactive/interrupt-based turns without changing the core sequential turn model.

Design (Option B from discussion):

```json
"triggers": {
  "on_discard": {
    "claim_window": {
      "eligible": "all_except_current",
      "actions": ["chi", "pon", "kan", "ron"],
      "priority": ["ron", "kan", "pon", "chi"],
      "timeout": 10,
      "default": "pass"
    }
  }
}
```

How it works: after apply_action, engine checks if any trigger matches the action type. If so, enters a mini-simultaneous collection phase. Eligible players submit a claim or pass. Server collects all responses (with timeout). Resolves by priority list. If someone claims, they become the active player. If everyone passes, normal turn order resumes.

Composable — works for any game with interrupt mechanics:
- Mahjong: trigger on discard → chi/pon/ron window
- Uno jump-in: trigger on play → same-card window
- Magic-style: trigger on spell → counter window
- Auction: trigger on bid → raise-or-pass window

Games without triggers behave exactly as today. No changes to alternating/round_robin/simultaneous turn order types.

Deliverables: (1) Schema addition for triggers section. (2) Engine: post-action trigger check. (3) Server: mini-simultaneous collection with timeout. (4) Priority resolution logic. (5) Update Mahjong definition to use triggers. (6) Tests.
design: Option B: action triggers. Lightest touch — turn system unchanged, triggers declared in game def, engine pauses for claim windows only when triggered.
close_reason: Fully implemented: schema, Rust engine, Python engine, server protocol with timeouts, 26 new tests (13 Rust + 13 Python), cross-impl test vectors, Mahjong definition updated. All existing tests pass, zero regressions.
